articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About Feeling Distant From God? Psalm 42-43
articles.excerpt: When your soul is cast down and God feels far away, these two psalms teach you how to pray honestly, preach truth to yourself, and anchor your hope in Christ.

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About Confessing Sin? Psalm 51
articles.excerpt: David didn't see the problem with his own behavior until Nathan the prophet confronted him. Psalm 51 and what it looks like to pray when we've fallen.
articles.verse_quote: Have mercy on me, O God, according to your steadfast love; according to your abundant mercy blot out my transgressions.

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About How to Pray? Psalm 145
articles.excerpt: If prayer is learning to speak with God, we should begin the same way Jesus began: with adoration, not requests. Psalm 145 and two simple ways to pray Scripture back to God.
articles.verse_quote: I will extol you, my God and King, and bless your name forever and ever... Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised, and his greatness is unsearchable.

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About Joy in Christ? The Book of Philippians
articles.excerpt: Stepping back from the phrase-by-phrase study to hear Philippians the way its first readers did — as one letter, read straight through, from a man in chains who could not stop rejoicing.
articles.verse_quote: Rejoice in the Lord always; again I will say, rejoice.

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About Contentment? Philippians 4:10-23
articles.excerpt: Paul learned to be content whether in plenty or in need — and he tells us plainly where that strength came from. Philippians 4:10-23 on contentment, gospel partnership, and God's promise to...
articles.verse_quote: I have learned, in whatever situation I am, to be content. I know how to be brought low, and I know how to abound. In any and every circumstance, I have learned the secret of facing plenty and hunger, abundance and need.

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About Renewing Your Mind? Philippians 4:8-9
articles.excerpt: What fills your mind shapes your life, the same way food shapes your body. Philippians 4:8-9 and the eight "whatevers" that describe the mind of Christ.
articles.verse_quote: Finally, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is just, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is commendable, if there is any excellence, if there is anything worthy of praise, think about these things.

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About Anxiety? Philippians 4:6-7
articles.excerpt: Anxiety isn't dealt with by force of will alone — it has to be replaced. Philippians 4:6-7 on prayer, supplication, thanksgiving, and the peace that surpasses understanding.
articles.verse_quote: Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God.

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About Standing Firm? Philippians 4:1-5
articles.excerpt: Unity, joy, gentleness, and hope don't come from circumstances. Philippians 4:1-5 grounds all four in a single fact: the Lord is near.
articles.verse_quote: Therefore, my brothers, whom I love and long for, my joy and crown, stand firm thus in the Lord, my beloved.

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About Who We Imitate? Philippians 3:17-21
articles.excerpt: You are imitating someone right now, whether you've noticed it or not. Philippians 3:17-21 on godly examples, enemies of the cross, and the citizenship that shapes how we live.
articles.verse_quote: Brothers, join in imitating me, and keep your eyes on those who walk according to the example you have in us.

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About Pressing On? Philippians 3:12-16
articles.excerpt: Paul, the apostle who wrote half the New Testament, flatly refuses to say he has arrived. Philippians 3:12-16 on why the Christian life is a race run to the very end.
articles.verse_quote: Not that I have already obtained this or am already perfect, but I press on to make it my own, because Christ Jesus has made me his own.

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About Gaining Christ? Philippians 3:8-11
articles.excerpt: Thirty years after his conversion, in a Roman prison, Paul still says the same thing he said on the Damascus road: everything else is rubbish compared to Christ.
articles.verse_quote: Indeed, I count everything as loss because of the surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord.

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About Counting Everything as Loss? Philippians 3:1-7
articles.excerpt: Paul had every credential a first-century Jew could want — and he moved every single one of them from the gain column to the loss column. What made him do the accounting that way?
articles.verse_quote: Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you is no trouble to me and is safe for you.

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About Genuine Christian Concern? Philippians 2:19-24
articles.excerpt: Paul had just handed the Philippians an impossible standard: have the mind of Christ. Now he shows them a real, ordinary, imperfect man who is actually living it — and asks whether our lives...
articles.verse_quote: I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon so that I too may be cheered by news of you.

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About the Humility of Christ? Philippians 2:5-11
articles.excerpt: An ancient hymn about a God who refused to grasp at His own glory, and was lifted higher than anyone in history because of it.
articles.verse_quote: "He did not count equality with God a thing to be grasped."

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About Christian Identity? Philippians 1:1-2
articles.excerpt: It's easy to read past a letter's opening greeting. Paul packs four load-bearing truths about identity and the church into just two verses.
articles.verse_quote: "Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are at Philippi."

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About Godly Grief vs. Worldly Grief? 1 Samuel 26
articles.excerpt: David spares Saul's life for the second time. Saul says "I have sinned" for at least the third time. Same words, same tears — and it still leads nowhere.
articles.verse_quote: "Do not destroy him, for who can put out his hand against the Lord's anointed?"

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About Being Rejected for Doing Good? 1 Samuel 23
articles.excerpt: David saves an entire city from ruin. The moment danger turns his way, that same city is ready to hand him over. A hard story about what it costs to do good.
articles.verse_quote: "And David and his men went to Keilah and fought with the Philistines."

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About Partial Obedience? Lessons from Saul and the Amalekites
articles.excerpt: King Saul comes back from battle certain he's done well. He obeyed almost everything God commanded — and that "almost" cost him the kingdom.
articles.verse_quote: "To obey is better than sacrifice."

articles.title: What Does Psalm 1 Mean? The Blessed Man, the Wicked Man, and You
articles.excerpt: Psalm 1 describes a blessed man who never sins and a wicked man who perishes, with no third option offered. If that doesn't sound like you yet, that's not the end of the story.
articles.verse_quote: "Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the wicked."

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About the Parable of the Sower?
articles.excerpt: Jesus told a story about a farmer, some seed, and four kinds of ground. It's also one of the most searching questions he ever put to a crowd: when the word of God lands on you, what kind of soil are you?
articles.verse_quote: "A sower went out to sow."

articles.title: What Does the Bible Say About Adultery and the Seventh Commandment?
articles.excerpt: Adultery has touched nearly every family in some way. Jesus says the seventh commandment was never just about the act itself — it starts in the heart, long before it reaches the hand.
articles.verse_quote: "You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall not commit adultery.’"
